enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 211–221 regulate the agent’s duties in conducting the principal’s business, required skill and diligence, accounts and communication, conflicts and secret profits, retention of sums, payment of receipts, remuneration and lien.

Definition: These provisions impose fiduciary and operational duties on an agent and define the agent’s corresponding rights to remuneration and lien.

Ingredients:
1. Identify the agency business and the agent’s mandate.
2. Assess skill, diligence, accounts and communication duties.
3. Identify any self-dealing, undisclosed benefit or conflict.
4. Determine when remuneration becomes due and whether misconduct affects entitlement.
5. Apply the statutory lien rule where the agent holds the principal’s property or money.
examples: An agent conducts the principal’s business for personal benefit without the principal’s consent; sections 215–216 permit the principal to claim the benefit obtained through the unauthorised self-dealing.

keyTakeaways: Sections 211–221 regulate the agent’s duties in conducting the principal’s business, required skill and diligence, accounts and communication, conflicts and secret profits, retention of sums, payment of receipts, remuneration and lien.
These provisions impose fiduciary and operational duties on an agent and define the agent’s corresponding rights to remuneration and lien.
